parts.note: P stands for piano, the musical direction to play quietly
to increase something is to raise it, as with a price or a wage

explanation.surface: Someone at a concert murmurs a request for the audience to clap louder.
explanation.definitionFit: Applause is the audible expression of approval, which is what acclaim or commendation amounts to.

parts.note: read as standing in for a famous person, but literally a stand that holds up a statue so it is raised high and seen by all

explanation.surface: An understudy or stand-in for a celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand for' tempts you to read 'represent', but the stand is a physical support, and the 'prominent figure' is a statue lifted on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A plinth or base that raises a statue or bust is a support for a figure placed on display, hence also an idiom for admiring someone excessively.

clue.text: Reliable account by copper on charge

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a rate is a charge or fee, as in the going rate

explanation.surface: A trustworthy report from a police officer who is booking a suspect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman, but it is the metal, giving its chemical symbol CU.
explanation.definitionFit: Accurate information is correct and exact, so it can be depended upon.

clue.text: Right link found by female detective

parts.note: she is the female pronoun
to lock is to join or link together, as in interlocking parts

explanation.surface: A woman investigator uncovers the correct connection in a case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detective' points to the fictional Baker Street sleuth; 'found by' is just a link placing the right and link pieces after the female one.
explanation.definitionFit: Holmes is the most famous fictional sleuth, so his first name stands for any investigator.

indicators.note: one thing trailing another follows behind it, so the fish word comes after the shoal word

parts.note: a shoal is a crowd or group, like a gang
a ling is a long, slender sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A skeletal fish swims along at the back of a school of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall, thin, awkward person is all angles and skinny limbs, which is what bony describes.

clue.text: Changing Iran is a top objective

indicators.note: the letters of these four words are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Reforming Iran is a foreign-policy goal of the highest priority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changing' rearranges IRAN IS A TOP; 'objective' looks like an adjective (impartial) but is the noun, a goal.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambition or goal one aims at is an objective.

clue.text: Returns vote with a good race

indicators.note: returns means the run of words for vote, a and good is read backwards

parts.note: a poll is a vote

explanation.surface: An election official reports the vote count along with a fine running contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returns' looks like election results, but it turns POLL + A + G backwards, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast ride or run at top speed is a race, as when a horse sprints flat out.

parts.note: sounds like a person leaning to the political right, but describes printed letters that slope rightwards

explanation.surface: A person whose politics drift towards conservatism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' suggests a person and 'right' politics, but here a character is a printed letter and the slope is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloping type used for emphasis leans to the right, unlike upright roman type.

clue.text: Reach, admitted, hard part of town

indicators.note: something admitted is let inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: to get to a place is to reach it
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone finally arrives at a tough district of the city and confesses it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitted' puts H inside GET TO.
explanation.definitionFit: A poor, segregated quarter of a city where a minority group lives is a district or area of town.

indicators.note: reportedly signals what is heard said, so the word for canal is taken by its sound

parts.note: a duct is a tube or channel, as the body's canals are also called ducts

explanation.surface: Someone fell into a waterway, so the rumour goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canal' tempts a waterway, but it is a bodily channel, a duct.
explanation.definitionFit: To dip or dunk someone under water is to plunge them in.

clue.text: Small tablet before senility gives release

parts.note: a pill is a tablet of medicine
age here means old age, the time of senility

explanation.surface: A small pill taken before dementia sets in brings relief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'release' looks like freeing someone, but here it means an escape of liquid; 'before' is just a link setting out the order.
explanation.definitionFit: A spill or leak is an escape of liquid, an accidental release of it.

indicators.note: taking means the first word swallows the other, holding it inside

parts.note: crusty and surly both mean bad-tempered and gruff
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A grumpy man on drugs, that's for certain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking ecstasy' reads as drug use; in fact the E is put inside SURLY.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverb of certainty, used to say something is beyond question.

parts.note: seems to describe an ardent lover, but taken literally it is someone whose passion is setting fire to things

explanation.surface: A person consumed by intense desire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burning passion' is normally figurative ardour; here it is literal, a love of starting fires.
explanation.definitionFit: A criminal who deliberately starts fires is literally passionate about burning.

clue.text: Expert is sceptical, strangely not caught

indicators.note: strangely says the letters of the words is and sceptical are rearranged
not tells you a letter is left out of that pool before rearranging

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A professional is oddly doubtful, though not fooled.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove C (caught, from 'not caught') from the letters of IS SCEPTICAL; 'strangely' then rearranges what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: A person with deep knowledge of one narrow field is an authority on it.

indicators.note: clearing up a mess means sorting it out, so these letters are put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone predicts they will make only a tiny profit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clearing' reads as netting a sum after costs, the sense the surface trades on; really it signals the anagram that makes NTICIPATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To look forward to something as likely to happen is to foresee or expect it.

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters of so and gather go wild into a new order

explanation.surface: Food is scarce, so go out and forage for nuts!
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' looks like the food to gather, but it is the signal to rearrange SO GATHER.
explanation.definitionFit: A dearth or lack of food is what a famine is.

clue.text: Old boy's story gripping cold bar

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil, plus the S of the possessive

indicators.note: gripping means holding something tightly inside, so the cold letter sits within the story word

parts.note: a tale is a story
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A former pupil's thrilling tale about a chilly pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gripping' looks like an adjective meaning exciting; it puts C inside TALE.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar is a barrier or hindrance, something that blocks the way.

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative, the British political party
arousal is a state of excitement

explanation.surface: Thrills generated by the Tory political party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party' looks political, next to 'Conservative', but the definition means a drinking session; 'by' just places C beside AROUSAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A drunken, rowdy celebration is a party, a binge.

parts.note: reads as intense worry, but literally means fear of being up high

explanation.surface: A state of great nervousness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High' looks like a degree of anxiety; it is the altitude that is feared.
explanation.definitionFit: A phobia of heights is literally an anxiety about high places.

indicators.note: after places the word for works behind the word for surgery

parts.note: op is short for operation, a surgical procedure
to work something, as in employing it, is to use it

explanation.surface: A patient has jobs to do once the operation is over.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Works' is the definition, artistic compositions; the second is the verb, giving USES.
explanation.definitionFit: Musical compositions are numbered as opus 1, opus 2, so they are a composer's works.

indicators.note: in tells you the letters sit within the run of words Colombo got another

explanation.surface: In Sri Lanka's former capital, someone acquired a second capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Colombo' suggests Sri Lanka, but the answer is the Colombian capital, which is hidden across those words.
explanation.definitionFit: The city is the seat of government of Colombia, its capital.

indicators.note: following places the word for premier behind the word for dupe

parts.note: to do someone is to cheat or dupe them
main and premier both mean chief or leading

explanation.surface: A nation's prime minister comes after a con man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'premier' looks like a prime minister; it is the adjective meaning chief, MAIN. The 's is read as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm or territory ruled by one sovereign is a country.

clue.text: Poor sap, possibly, left after marriage offer

indicators.note: after places L behind the rearranged letters
possibly signals the letters of poor and sap may be rearranged another way

explanation.surface: A hapless fool is abandoned once he asks someone to marry him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges POOR SAP into PROPOSA; 'marriage offer' is the definition, not part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking someone for their hand in marriage is the offer made when one pops the question.

clue.text: Hollow, rubbish Tory leader in move

indicators.note: in puts the rubbish letters and the Tory leader inside the word for move

parts.note: go means a move or turn, as in a game
rot means rubbish or nonsense

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word Tory

explanation.surface: A Conservative chief makes an empty, worthless move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tory leader' looks like the party head, but it gives the T that starts 'Tory'.
explanation.definitionFit: A small cave is a hollow in rock.

indicators.note: goes wrong signals the letters of cops and raid are scrambled into another order

explanation.surface: A police swoop is botched by chaotic officers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes wrong' rearranges COPS RAID.
explanation.definitionFit: Happening irregularly and unpredictably at scattered intervals is what erratic means.

indicators.note: say signals a spoken sound, so only how the word for plug is pronounced is used

parts.note: to caulk is to plug a gap with filler, as on a boat's seams
US is short for United States, so American

explanation.surface: An American gives an example of a stopper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like 'for example' but is the sound indicator: CAULK sounds like CAUC.
explanation.definitionFit: A closed meeting of party members to choose candidates or policy is a political convention.

clue.text: Brown back in period of decline

indicators.note: in places the turned brown word inside the word for period

parts.note: a stage is a period or phase of development

indicators.note: back means the word for brown is read backwards

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour

explanation.surface: Gordon Brown returns during an era of economic downturn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns TAN into NAT and 'in' places it. 'Brown' suggests Gordon Brown, the former UK prime minister, and 'decline' a political slump.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceasing to develop or grow and becoming sluggish is a way of going downhill.

clue.text: 'Dallas' maybe, for the audience is corn

indicators.note: for the audience means what the listeners hear spoken, so the sound is used

parts.note: Dallas was a long-running TV soap opera, an example of a serial

explanation.surface: The TV soap is, for viewers, rather corny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corn' suggests something hackneyed, as with the soap; it is the grain.
explanation.definitionFit: Maize and wheat are grain crops of the kind called corn in Britain.
